feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear progression, relevant scope, and good public-sector positioning. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some structural overlap that reduces sharpness and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression at NACo culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale and specificity: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” “50+ internal publishers” adds credibility.  
- Relevant, modern skill mix: combines strategy, CMS/platform delivery, analytics, AI-enabled search, and content operations effectively.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve structure and readability.  
- Tighten wording for impact: many bullets start with “Led,” “Built,” or “Developed,” and several points are long. Vary verbs and shorten bullets to emphasize outcomes over responsibilities.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation style is inconsistent across bullets; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead. No obvious misspellings, but standardize capitalization and formatting (e.g., “Coleman DAVIS” vs normal title case).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with sharper outcomes and a tighter opening line.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more distinctive positioning tied to public-sector/platform leadership.
- Tighten the list of responsibilities into 3–4 priority themes and foreground scale or complexity.
- Use parallel phrasing: “web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial operations, and AI-enabled discovery.”
- Possible rewrite: “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for high-volume, mission-driven public-sector organizations. Builds the governance, analytics, editorial, and multimedia operations that support complex communications at scale, including Drupal platform modernization, reporting infrastructure, and AI-enabled search and content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” repeats the subtitle’s positioning; vary the phrasing.
- “Governance models/content operations/analytics infrastructure” closely duplicates Core Competencies and should stay high-level here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if tightened around distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases already covered elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording for consistency: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications leadership
- Replace generic items with more specific, senior-level language: AI-enabled search and structured content systems • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia, studio, and livestream production
- Consider ordering by current strategic value and recency: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, automation, communications, multimedia
- Use “web” instead of “website” for a more executive, CV-consistent style

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” “AI-enabled…experiences,” and “multimedia production” repeat the header almost verbatim
- This section also overlaps with Topline Skills; keep Core Competencies higher-level and let Topline/Technical sections carry tools and channel detail
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a compressed portfolio section and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Retitle as “Selected Recent Projects” and use parallel, concise phrasing: action + platform/output + purpose.
- Trim repetitive wording like “built/developed/designed” and reduce stacked descriptors; e.g., “AI-enabled legislative search using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Standardize style and punctuation: use sentence fragments or full sentences consistently; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for cleaner CV style.
- If space allows, add one concrete result, audience, or scale metric to 1–2 projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in recent roles.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider keeping that and shortening or rotating the more redundant entries.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and “Recent Projects.” Make it sharper by emphasizing strategic ownership, technical depth, and any measurable outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a stronger lead: “Serve as strategic communications and digital platforms consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, content operations, and AI-enabled search.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-focused lines; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet about improving cross-channel communications operations.
- Add outcomes where possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/publishers supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search/discovery improvements, efficiency gains, or reduced publishing friction.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting” with “Built and maintained Drupal/front-end solutions for large public-facing sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI-enabled search, microsites, and campaign storytelling are already echoed in “Recent Projects”; keep this entry higher-level and reserve specifics there.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement also repeat the summary and NACo role; focus on what is new in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine scope + flagship achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused: add engagement, list growth, campaign performance, or production volume if available; otherwise trim “tens of thousands/thousands” language.
- Rephrase operational bullets to show business value: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, reducing external production reliance and expanding advocacy/event content capacity”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry at the strategic/enterprise level.
- Video production/studio language may duplicate the footer projects and earlier NACo roles unless framed as leadership/build-out.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong mid-career progression item, but it overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and show what changed under your leadership, with metrics if available.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scope/results: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-based: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add a concrete workflow/editorial impact metric if possible: publishing volume, turnaround time, campaign cadence, stakeholder teams supported, or engagement growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning…” and “improved digital publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language; keep this role focused on execution and channel operations.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this as scaling/formalizing the program, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter and more differentiated, emphasizing strategic leadership rather than repeating broad communications language.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Content governance and editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and journey-based content strategy
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel operating model leadership” if you want a more senior, systems-oriented tone.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this category to scale/results already proven in experience (10,000+ page migration, 50+ publishers, 3.5M annual page views) rather than adding more abstract skill labels.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is weaker than “communications” and overlaps with multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s currently a mixed list of platforms, methods, and tools with heavy overlap against both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize recent, higher-value capabilities and reduce older/basic items.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool dump to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop or de-emphasize “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery”; these are better housed in Technical + IT unless the role explicitly requires hands-on coding prominence.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Enterprise CMS platforms (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)” for concision.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work elsewhere, such as “supporting large public-facing sites and modernization initiatives.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- Platform/tool details substantially duplicate the Technical + IT section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic value and decision-making, not repeat the full stack.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting”
- Trim to the most differentiating tools and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with a sharper phrase like “SEO, UX and conversion performance analysis”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and conversion performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly
- “Leadership reporting” also overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; use one strategic phrase here and leave the tool inventory to Technical + IT

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and tied to delivery environments rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Virtual event operations • End-to-end multimedia workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a broader, more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to avoid sounding tactical.
- Consider swapping “Studio operations” for “Multi-camera studio systems” or “Studio buildout and operations” if you want to reflect the in-house studio achievement from the 2022–2024 role.
- Keep this skills block focused on capabilities; save examples, scale, and outcomes for recent work experience bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- This section also echoes NACo experience bullets on studio buildout and event/video production, so avoid repeating exact wording.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills almost exactly. This item should either add nuance (depth/level) or be tightened to emphasize strongest, most recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strength/relevance: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling depth: “Drupal (advanced) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, make it more outcome-oriented via scope labels rather than just a list: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; lightweight publishing: GitHub Pages.”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it’s not materially used in recent roles; it reads lighter-weight than the rest.
- Keep platform names only here; save modernization/governance language for experience bullets where impact is already shown.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” especially Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages.
- “CMS modernization” is already covered elsewhere; don’t add it here unless you remove it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it feel more current and implementation-focused, with emphasis on tools actually supporting recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize the list: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent projects; it can make the stack feel dated.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier for impact/context, e.g. “for Drupal-based sites, campaign microsites, analytics tagging and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” especially HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations and workflow automation.
- Consider using this section for tool specificity only, while leaving broader capability language in Topline Skills.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for clarity: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add light context instead of only listing tools, e.g.: “Workflow automation, project tracking and cross-team collaboration tools: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If any were used to build operational systems, prioritize those 3–5 tools and drop weaker/general collaboration apps

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Slack and Teams are collaboration tools, not workflow systems; they dilute the section unless reframed
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear elsewhere, so this item should emphasize tool stack breadth, not repeat capability claims

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize system breadth and avoid overstating older or less central tools.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform names for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If these were hands-on admin/build tools, consider adding one qualifier: “campaign operations, newsletter publishing, audience journeys”
- Only keep all three if each was used meaningfully; otherwise prioritize the most recent/relevant platform(s), especially Dynamics 365 and Higher Logic

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused
- “Engagement” may feel vague given “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies; “Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms” is clearer

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently a generic list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” It would be stronger if grouped more strategically and framed around analysis/optimization rather than repeating exact platform names elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Recast as grouped capabilities for readability: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO, A/B testing, dashboarding”
- Consider tightening the title to “Analytics, Reporting & Optimization” to better match the actual content.
- If space allows, replace one generic term with a stronger capability: swap “Dashboarding” for “KPI reporting” or “Performance analysis.”
- Keep only the tools most tied to recent impact; GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are the strongest given the 2022–2024 NACo role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; keep one version shorter or differentiate this one as tools-only.
- “SEO” and “A/B testing” are not evidenced elsewhere; keep them only if you can support them in experience bullets or projects.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational impact, team-building, and distinct early-career contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcomes where possible: “Supported a major website refresh” → specify platform, scope, traffic, or launch result if known.
- Make multimedia contribution more concrete: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates that expanded recurring digital advocacy/content programming.”
- Tighten management phrasing: “provided day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate” → “supervised a digital media associate’s daily production and publishing work.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on launching or establishing the format, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating generic workflow language already used in later NACo roles unless you can show this was the initial buildout phase.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo multimedia roles. Emphasize the “first podcast” achievement and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; produced digital and multimedia content to extend program visibility.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and sharpen ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to” with stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “supported,” depending on actual ownership.
- If possible, add one concrete measure: number of episodes launched, audiences served, or types of projects/campaigns supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia/video language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Keep this entry focused on research/program support plus the podcast launch, which is the clearest differentiator.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed skills/responsibilities list than a crisp tools section. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as software/platform proficiency only; move workflow-type phrases out.
- Suggested rewrite: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast recording/editing • Livestream production tools”
- If accurate, replace generic “Livestream production tools” with named platforms/equipment (e.g., OBS, StreamYard, vMix, PTZ systems) to make the skill more concrete.
- If multimedia is not a hiring priority, shorten further to just the core tools and let work experience carry the impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” and “Studio operations” elsewhere.
- “Podcast production” is already evidenced in older experience; keep only if you want to preserve breadth, not depth.
